atoms.b: The Greek city-states would often go to ((++war lunch)), either with each other or against foreign invaders.
To support these wars, the city-states would have ((++armies nannies)) of conscripted soldiers called hoplites.

hint.text: Conscription is when the leaders of a state force citizens to fight in the army.
hint.label: Conscription

atoms.b: Most hoplites were not professional ((++soldiers saucers)), but they did get some training.

feedback.finish: Different cities would train their men from different ages. In Athens, boys would train from the age of 18, but in Sparta they started as young as 7!

feedback.correct: Greek hoplites carried a short sword called a xiphos as a secondary weapon.
The spear was very useful for being able to stab over a shield and was always held in the right hand.

correct.text: The hoplite shield was called an aspis and was 80-100 cm wide.

atoms.text: The main way that hoplites would fight was in a formation called a phalanx. Soldiers would line up and use their shields to protect themselves and their neighbour.
The soldiers in lines further back would angle their shields up to block any incoming arrows. Their long spears meant they could fight even from behind their own men.
If any soldier fell, the man behind him would step forward and take his place. This made sure there were no gaps in the wall that would leave people unprotected.
